title: Answer: a choice is deterministic settling and freedom is irreducibility, shown on a stand-in

statements.text: The rule is fixed and draws no random number, so the whole state at one beat fixes the next. Vibe answers the free will problem with compatibilism: a choice is the state a self settles into, the same way every run, and freedom is measured irreducibility, since no cheap predictor reads the choice before it is made. Agency is the self as a cause: a different self under the same urge settles elsewhere. This is shown only on a stand-in, the deliberation engine, because the working rule forms no self to choose yet.
statements.scope: a known attractor model and an older reversible rule, not the working rule

standing.reason: vibe's own answer to the questionnaire

sources.quote: In the model a choice is that kind of settling, the same way every run.
The model gives it a mechanism: choice as deterministic settling, freedom as measured irreducibility.
A different self under the same urge settles elsewhere, so the self’s own structure is a cause of the choice and not a channel for the urge.
The future is fixed and still has to be lived to be known.
